title: St. Bernard neighborhood and the Francs Amis Hall
summary: Albert describes his unchanged boyhood street and the hall a block away where he sat in with Manuel Perez, Chris Kelly and other bands.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Oh, I see. So, well, now, where you were going is near St. Bernard Avenue.
It's two blocks from St. Bernard. One long block.
What was that street like when you were growing up?

It's the same way now as it was then. There's no difference. I looked at all the old houses yesterday. There has been no improvement. Maybe just a paid job. But it's the same identical way it's always been. And that's over 64 years.
Did you play on that street?

Sure, I played. It was an old hall called the Frans Amie Hall which is about a block, a full block from where I was born. And I used to love to go there because I'd climb up the steps and go to the bands used to play up the stairs that weren't in the pianos. And I would go up there and sit down with Amanda Perez and sometimes it'd be Chris Kelly or all the new railroad runners. Whatever band was there, I was able to get in because everybody knew me and called me but I was this little fella down with the little creole he was coming in and just letting in. I guess I've always been a lack of a fella and I have always been able to make friends on the spur of the moment. There's no problem for me to meet a man today and become closely acquainted with him as a friend.
